_note: Booklet A / MCQ answers for the 2026 Chinese prelim corpus, read off the
scan by eye for every one of the ten schools -- not just the gaps.
Unlike the Science and English prelim keys (review/prelim-mcq-key.json,
review/en-mcq-key.json), none of these ten schools' keys is typed: every one
is a scanned grid, and nine of the ten carry a heavy diagonal watermark
('SgTestPaper.com' / 'More Papers') that sits directly across several answer
cells on every school's grid. A position-based OCR reader tuned against one
school's cell geometry would need retuning against the other nine's, and the
watermark defeats plain OCR on the cells it crosses regardless -- so the whole
grid was read visually against the rendered 300 dpi page instead of building
a geometry reader for a one-off table shape repeated across ten schools.
Where the watermark crosses a cell, the digit is still legible: the white
typeface prints through the black watermark shape with the digit's ink
surviving as a white cutout, confirmed against a 1.2x-2x crop of that cell
for every obscured answer below. TaoNan and RedSwastika have no watermark at
all and were read directly off the full page.
See CLAUDE.md section 1.6.1 for why a wrong digit here is the worst failure
in this project: there is no partial credit to soften it, and the child is
simply told she was wrong when she was right. Every entry below was read
once, then the obscured cells were re-read a second time from a zoomed crop
before being committed.
build/cn_prelim_key.py treats this file as authoritative for these ten
schools (there is no competing OCR read to cross-check it against, unlike
prelim_key.py's schools where most of the corpus was typed) and validates it
only against build/cn_prelim_index.py's question inventory -- every answer
must be within the option range indexing found for that question, and every
question the paper actually asks must have an entry.
